context.purpose: Publish small structured reports as standalone HTML and editable Word DOCX.
context.assumptions: Plain single-space text, one-row table headers, bounded local RGB/RGBA PNG imagery; default Pandoc typography.
context.constraints: Up to 32 sections,128 content blocks, 65536 characters,8 images; heading levels 1–3 start at 1 and increase by at most 1. No authored markup/scripts/styles/templates/filters.
context.inspection: Compare ordered headings, paragraph text, complete table cells and image alt/media bytes in HTML, independent OOXML and fresh native DOCX JSON readback. Inspect the report-summary loss policy and generated documents.
context.recovery: INVALID_REPORT_TABLE needs rectangular rows; INVALID_HEADING_ORDER needs an outline starting at 1. INVALID_REPORT_IMAGE needs an absolute regular plain RGB/RGBA PNG. INVALID_REPORT_TEXT needs single-space plain text. INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND needs configured Pandoc; retained logs and failed result explain native faults.

workflow.scope: Report jobs run within the common workflow with independently verified publications; no arbitrary document-format import.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure expressions and finite visits resolve before report planning.

lifecycle.timeout: One total deadline covers runtime/API probes, both writers, fresh readback and verification.
lifecycle.cancellation: Owned native processes use shared cancellation; check again before publication.
lifecycle.logs: Retain authored/effective plans, captured PNGs/digests, trusted AST, runtime, commands, stdout/stderr, HTML/DOCX, extracted readback media and failed/succeeded results.
lifecycle.verification: Independent HTML parser and standard-library ZIP/OOXML relationships/cells/headings/image geometry/media checks compare with authored values; fresh Pandoc DOCX reader repeats the semantic check. Every image source is captured as a bounded regular file.

losses: Default typography/pagination only; no exact layout, rich text or accessibility certification.

losses: Browser rendering is not a pixel-equivalence contract.
